analysis.investment_thesis: Ather Energy is a pre-profit EV startup with negative EBIT every single year since inception — the Magic Formula cannot be applied, and at 10x P/S with deeply negative returns on capital, there is no margin of safety. Revenue growth is real but irrelevant until the company demonstrates it can convert sales into earnings.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 130% over 5 years (INR 35 Cr → 2,255 Cr) shows genuine market traction
Positive gross margin of 19.43% confirms some unit-level economics exist
Low Debt/Equity of 0.16 and recent IPO equity infusion (equity surged to 2,721 Cr in 2025) reduce near-term insolvency risk
key_risks: Negative EBIT of -581 Cr in 2025 — Magic Formula requires positive EBIT; this company is unrankable
Free cash flow negative every year for 5 years (-1,060 Cr in 2025), fully dependent on external capital to survive
Valued at 10x sales with no earnings path in sight — any slowdown in revenue growth or funding could be catastrophic
red_flags: EBIT has never been positive in 6 years of history — Magic Formula produces no valid output
Operating Cash Flow negative all 5 years (0/5 positive); cash burn accelerating
ROE of -156% and ROCE of -65.7% — capital destruction at scale
EV/EBITDA of -50x and Forward P/E of -79x: valuation metrics are literally nonsensical
Net losses grew from -220 Cr (2020) to peak -1,060 Cr (2024); only modest improvement to -812 Cr in 2025
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying the Magic Formula to Ather Energy is a non-starter. Earnings Yield = EBIT / EV requires positive EBIT. With operating income at -581 Cr in 2025 and an Enterprise Value of roughly 34,500 Cr, the earnings yield is approximately -1.7% — deeply negative. Return on Capital = EBIT / (Net Working Capital + Net Fixed Assets) is equally meaningless. The company has destroyed capital every year since 2020, and the cumulative free cash outflow exceeds 3,270 Cr. This is not a business that earns high returns on tangible capital; it is a business that consumes capital to subsidize growth.

The only faint green shoot is the 19.43% gross margin, which suggests the product itself isn't being sold below variable cost. But gross margin is miles away from EBIT profitability when operating losses run at -26% of revenue in 2025. At INR 2,255 Cr in revenue and INR 34,295 Cr in market cap, investors are paying 10x sales for a business that is still years from breakeven. Greenblatt's framework rewards companies that earn high returns on capital at cheap prices — Ather offers neither. This is pure speculation on a future that may or may not materialize.
